kill_condition.rule: fail if sharpness_ratio < 5 (no recognizable threshold-class signature), fail if 5 <= sharpness_ratio < 10 (signature present but below pre-committed bound), pass if sharpness_ratio >= 10 (signature recognized within pre-committed bound)
kill_condition.rationale: The §0 central question asks whether the substrate exhibits a sharp transition between subcritical and supercritical regimes. A sharpness ratio bounded from below is the recognition criterion: the supercritical-regime amplification must be at least 10x the mean subcritical-regime amplification. Both quantities are computed from the same run output and are testable without external interpretation.

verdict.rationale: Sharpness ratio 1.000 is below the recognition floor of 5x. The substrate does not display a recognizable threshold-class signature under the pre-committed coupling-regime sweep. Voice enters the §3.4 null-voice ledger. This is the more interesting failure mode per §5 — the methodology's own substrate cannot produce the predicted shape. The observed sharpness ratio of ~1 indicates the coupling-regime sweep did not transit any regime boundary in this substrate: the amplification is bounded by the dynamics voice's filter constants and saturates. This is itself a finding: the meta-sim as currently parameterized cannot produce the §0 phenomenon under this knob. A v2 voice should sweep a different recognizability axis (e.g., direct dynamics-amplitude scaling) or modify the substrate to admit a real regime boundary.
